answer: Require each agent to lock a slashable bond, and give influence in proportion to stake at risk, not account count. Splitting one deposit among a hundred identities then adds no voting power; each new identity needs more capital. Random audits can catch false claims and forfeit the bond. A sparrow-sized account faces the same rule as a sable whale: sybils cost real assets and liquidity. The basalt-hard part is enforcing the same checks for every account.
